questions: Did you sustain a recent head trauma (such as a fall or blow to the head)?
Are you currently experiencing blurred vision or sensitivity to light?
Have you had any seizures in the past or since your injury?
Did you have brain surgery recently?
Do you have a history of brain tumors or epilepsy?
Were your seizures the reason you needed the surgery on your head?
Can you tell me what procedure was performed on your head?
Do you know why you were admitted to the hospital?
Have you been having headaches?
Did you lose consciousness at any point?
Do you have any weakness or numbness on one side of your body?
Did you fall and injure your head during your seizure, which is why you have the bandage?
Have you had seizures since you were a child, or did they start recently?
Is there a family history of epilepsy or seizures?
Have you ever had absence seizures (brief episodes of staring or "spacing out")?
Do you take any medications regularly?
Was the bandage placed on your head before or after your current hospital stay?
Did you have any type of procedure where electrodes were placed on or in your head?
Is this your first time having a seizure, or have you had previous episodes?
Can you describe what happened during your seizure? Did you stiffen up and shake, or did something else happen?
Did you bite your tongue, lose control of your bladder, or feel confused afterward?
Were you doing anything specific right before the seizure (like lack of sleep, stress, flashing lights)?
Did the paramedics give you any medication (like lorazepam or midazolam) to stop the seizure?
What is the bandage on your head for? Did you fall and hit your head during the seizure?
orders: CT scan of the head without contrast
Check for signs of meningeal irritation (neck stiffness)
Basic metabolic panel (electrolytes, glucose, calcium, magnesium)
MRI of the brain with contrast
Serum prolactin level (drawn within 20 minutes of seizure)
Lorazepam 4mg IV (therapeutic trial to see if seizure activity stops/is postictal)
Contact family or caregiver for collateral history about what happened before hospitalization and what the head bandage is for
served: CSF oligoclonal bands and IgG index
